description.value: Kamei Royale is BC's longest-running Japanese restaurant, open since 1972 with roots tracing back 150 years to Tsukiji, Japan, and widely credited as the birthplace of the BC Roll — Canada's first original sushi roll. Located in downtown Vancouver's Oceanic Plaza, it blends a traditional Japanese dining experience with a lively late-night karaoke stage open to any guest who orders a drink. A touring cyclist will find a full lunch and dinner menu, complimentary green tea during lunch, and underground parking available to restaurant guests.

bike_parking_detail: 1 rack within 100m: stands (3 spaces) at 97m. Total: 3 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is fully accessible and confirms the restaurant is open, with business hours, menus, and reservation info. OSM address (Unit 110 – 1066 West Hastings Street, Vancouver, BC V6E 3X2), phone (604-687-8588), and website URL all match the website content. No mention of bike parking, bike racks, washrooms, or water bottle refill was found on the site; online ordering and delivery are confirmed via the website navigation and text.
concerns: Minor hours discrepancy: OSM lists Sunday as 17:00–21:30, but the About page lists Sunday as 11:30 AM–2:30 PM and 4:00 PM–10:00 PM; the Karaoke/Delivery subpage lists Sunday as 5:00 PM–9:30 PM. Hours appear to vary across sources and may not be current — cyclists should call ahead.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, long-established, publicly accessible restaurant in downtown Vancouver with an active website and confirmed contact details. A useful stop for touring cyclists seeking a sit-down Japanese meal.
